column3: A three-story tower on a small island in the Nanming River in Guiyang, built in the Ming dynasty. It is a symbol of the city.
A hill park in the middle of Guiyang, with forest paths, a lake, a Buddhist temple and a lot of cheeky wild macaques.
A Ming-era walled town with stone streets, old gates and temples, where Han, Miao and other peoples have lived.
A shrine to Wang Yangming, the Ming philosopher who developed his famous ideas while living in exile in Guizhou.
Fish cooked in a tangy red broth of fermented tomatoes and chili. It is a Miao classic and one of Guizhou's best-loved dishes.
Thin pancakes wrapped around shredded vegetables, peanuts and sauces. They look like little dolls in white silk.
A Guiyang noodle dish with pork intestines, blood tofu and chili oil in a rich, spicy soup.
Little cubes of tofu grilled until they puff up, then filled with chili dip, a favorite street snack in Guiyang.
Sticky rice is a staple of Guizhou's festival tables, eaten with pickles, cured meat and spicy sauces.
Guizhou people love chili: fermented, dried, ground and cooked in sauces. It is the soul of the cuisine here.
Miao women wear heavy silver headdresses, necklaces and collars at festivals. Each piece is hammered by hand and tells a story.
The Dong people sing in many-voiced choirs without conductor or instruments, imitating birds, water and wind. It is UNESCO-listed.
A building in Zunyi where, in January 1935, Communist leaders held a key meeting during the Long March, a turning point in the party's history.
A small town by the Chishui River, known for the Moutai distilleries. The air there smells of fermenting sorghum.
Red cliffs, waterfalls and bamboo forests in a green valley, part of the UNESCO Danxia landform listing.
A river associated with a famous 1935 maneuver, in which the Red Army crossed the river four times to escape its pursuers.
China's best-known baijiu, made from sorghum and wheat in Maotai and aged for years, with a rich, savory aroma.
Rice noodles in a lamb broth, topped with slices of lamb, herbs and chili, a typical breakfast in Zunyi.
A local baijiu from Yaxi, with a long history, aged in earth cellars.
Baijiu is at the center of toasts and celebrations in Guizhou, and drinking customs are a big part of hospitality.
The most famous waterfall in China, about 70 meters high and 100 meters wide. A path leads behind the falls, where you can feel the spray.
A large cave system with an underground river, lakes and waterfalls, which can be explored by boat.
A thin rice-flour wrap filled with vegetables, meat and sauces, a snack from Anshun.
A cold jelly made from buckwheat, served in a spicy, sour sauce, refreshing in summer.
Ground opera is a ritual drama where performers in painted wooden masks act out ancient battles, originally brought by soldiers in the Ming dynasty.
The largest Miao village in China, with thousands of wooden stilt houses on a hillside. At night the whole slope glows with lights.
A Dong village with five drum towers, wind-and-rain bridges and wooden houses, in the valley of Southeast Guizhou.
A river town with old streets, stone gates and temples along the Wu River, which has been a transport hub for over 2,000 years.
Fish preserved with salt and sticky rice in jars for months. It is a Dong specialty with a strong, sour flavor.
The lusheng is a reed pipe of several bamboo tubes, played and danced to at Miao and Dong festivals.
One of China's largest caves, with huge halls full of stalagmites, columns and crystal-like formations.
Sticky rice balls, filled with sweet or savory fillings and served in a hot broth. A winter favorite.
Weining is a high plateau where buckwheat is grown, and its flour is made into noodles, pancakes and cakes.
A sacred Buddhist mountain with a rock tower that stands on its summit. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Rice noodles with meat and a spicy sauce, a breakfast staple in Tongren.
A tea grown in the cloud-covered Fanjing Mountain, known for a fresh and mellow taste.
A grand landscape of thousands of cone-shaped karst peaks that rise from green fields.
Rice noodles in a rich chicken broth, topped with shredded chicken, a Xingyi specialty.
Sticky rice dyed with plant juices in five colors, made by the Buyi people for festivals.
FAST, the world's largest single-dish radio telescope, sits in a natural karst bowl. It listens to faint signals from deep space.
A scenic area of emerald pools, small waterfalls and an old seven-arch bridge, among forests of Libo.
A famed green tea from Duyun, with slender leaves covered with fine hair and a fresh taste.
Fresh river fish from Libo, cooked in soup or in a tangy sauce.
Kiwi fruit from the cool highlands of Liupanshui are sweet and sour and are grown on a large scale.
